title: Manifest
description: GET /capabilities. What the add-on is, what it can do beyond the core, and what its fields mean. The schema is strict (field, operation and metric objects refuse an unknown key unless it begins x-); the backend's decode of it is tolerant.

contract_version.description: The wire contract major both ends speak. Contract 2: equality-checked, a mismatch is refused with CONTRACT_VERSION_MISMATCH.

kind.description: The closed kind list in registry/kinds.json; it keys the credential-scope denylist and the UI module.

features.description: Additive capabilities, listed in registry/features.json. An unknown name is skipped, never refused.

entitlement_schema.description: The fields of desired state Syndra may fill. Exactly one has role account.

^x-.description: Vendor data: ignored by the core, never used for a decision, shown raw on the target page.

label.description: The field's name for a person.

per_person.description: An operator may set this field for one person, over what roles give.

combine.description: How several roles' values for a limit combine. Unlimited dominates.

unlimited.description: The value that means no ceiling, e.g. "0".

^x-.description: Vendor data: ignored by the core, never used for a decision, shown raw on the target page.

id.description: The operation id, e.g. password.set; a name in registry/operations.json.

scope.description: The broadest scope the add-on offers it at; the backend narrows it to its own ceiling.

secret_params.description: Parameter names whose values are never persisted, logged or hashed.

available.description: The target can perform it right now.

params.description: A JSON Schema for the parameters, a UI hint only (labels, placeholders, an enum for a picker). The backend validates against its own policy and ignores this for any decision.

^x-.description: Vendor data: ignored by the core, never used for a decision, shown raw on the target page.

name.description: Lowercase, dot-namespaced; the first segment is the kind or product.

per_subject.description: Reported per person as well as in total.

^x-.description: Vendor data: ignored by the core, never used for a decision, shown raw on the target page.

dimensions.description: At most four, naming resources and never people.

against.description: A limit field of the same unit; the UI draws the gauge as a meter against the subject's observed limit.

^x-.description: Vendor data: ignored by the core, never used for a decision, shown raw on the target page.

Connection.description: How a member reaches the target; a storage fact. Absent when the deployment has not said.

protocol.description: What a member connects with, e.g. smb.

host.description: The name a member types, never the API URL.

Limits.description: What only the add-on knows. Syndra's own caps live in registry/constants.json and are never declared here.

subjects_per_plan.description: The most subjects one /plan may carry; above it the add-on answers PLAN_TOO_LARGE.

stats_buffer.description: Feature stats. How long a point stays buffered; default P90D, ceiling P400D.
